slides.title: Non-Type Template Parameters Concept
slides.prompt: Besides data types, templates can accept non-type parameters such as compile-time integer constants, pointers, references, and (since C++20) literal floating-point/class values.

slides.title: Non-Type Parameter Declaration
slides.prompt: Fill in the integer parameter type in the template parameter list.

slides.title: Requirement for Non-Type Parameters
slides.prompt: What restriction applies to non-type template arguments passed during instantiation?
options: They must be constant expressions known at compile time
They can be dynamic variables evaluated at runtime
They must always be unsigned integer types
They can only be passed by reference
slides.correctAnswer: They must be constant expressions known at compile time

slides.title: Default Non-Type Template Parameter
slides.prompt: Fill in the default value assignment for the non-type template argument.

slides.title: Type Distinctness with Non-Type Parameters
slides.prompt: Are StaticArray<int, 5> and StaticArray<int, 10> considered the same type by the compiler?
options: No, they are entirely distinct classes, and objects cannot be assigned to each other
Yes, because their element type T (int) is identical
Yes, size parameters are stripped after template compilation
Only if an implicit conversion operator is defined
slides.correctAnswer: No, they are entirely distinct classes, and objects cannot be assigned to each other

slides.title: std::array Non-Type Parameter Usage
slides.prompt: How does C++ standard library std::array<T, N> utilize non-type template parameters?
options: N specifies the fixed stack-allocated size of the array at compile time
N determines the dynamic initial capacity reserved on the heap
N controls the alignment offset in memory
N defines the thread-safety lock granularity
slides.correctAnswer: N specifies the fixed stack-allocated size of the array at compile time
